description:
This is the salsa/northstar replacement for the seal's barrier role and the precise thing the prototype deletion lacked (it produced a stale artifact that the backend then executed). DeriveTransportPlan (transport.rs:852-853) and MaterializeRoot both gate on SemanticClosed(root) purely to learn 'the executable frontier is COMPLETE'. Northstar: completeness is QUIESCENCE, not a per-root fact.

DO: make the root assemblers (DeriveTransportPlan, the MaterializeRoot assembler from fz-463.7) subscribe to the LIVE membership frontier (the analyzer's Activation/Executable presence facts + CallSiteTargets that now carry membership post-fz-463.4) and re-fire whenever a new executable JOINS the frontier or a member's content fact bumps. Drop the SemanticClosed gate. The assembler fans in the current frontier; if membership grows, the new member's presence fact re-wakes it; the drive only reaches Resolved at the true fixpoint, so the QUIESCENT artifact is complete. Crucially: artifacts are consumed (executed) only after the drive goes quiet (the compile entry drives to quiescence then reads), so a transiently-incomplete assembly is corrected before any consumer acts.

PROOF OBLIGATION: the assembler MUST re-fire on membership growth (the missing subscription is what caused the prototype's stale-artifact execution). Verify membership-growth wakes the assembler; converges_identically across schedules. One commit. Blocked by fz-463.7. Blocks fz-463.9.
title: [KEYSTONE] Root artifact assemblers converge by frontier-subscription + quiescence, not SemanticClosed
